Openreach taps Ciena for 1.6Tbps WaveLogic 6 technology
Optical upgrades will support Openreach's wholesale offering
UK broadband provider Openreach has tapped Ciena to expand its high-capacity connectivity services for UK wholesale customers.
In an announcement today (October 7), Ciena confirmed that Openreach has been deploying Ciena's Waveserver 1.6Tbps coherent technology into its Optical Spectrum Extended Access (OSEA) portfolio. The deployment is underpinned by Ciena's WaveLogic 6 (WL6) technology.
Openreach is using the technology to provide its wholesale customers with tailored network solutions serving specialist locations such as cable landing stations (CLS), access and backhaul services to core intersect nodes and data centers.
The company, a subsidiary of UK telecoms giant BT, is currently building out its full fiber network across the country and is on course to hit 25 million locations by the end of this year.
Ciena notes that its solution includes the deployment of 400G and 800G client traffic over dedicated 1.6Tbps wavelengths, with a 2RU chassis supporting up to 32 x 400G services. In simple terms, Ciena claims this significantly expands the range of high-capacity services Openreach can offer.
Beyond this, Openreach has also introduced national 800G services for the first time and creates a clear path to even faster services as customers’ needs grow.
According to Ciena, its Waveserver technology gives Openreach's wholesale customers "more flexible, tailored options for services that need to carry very large amounts of data."
The company added that Openreach's wholesale customers that are using the telco's fiber network will be able to support high-capacity connections between data centers, private cloud networks for businesses, and connections between international cable landing stations and data centers.
In addition to this, there will be greater resiliency using different fiber routes across the UK, plus additional capacity to support growth in cloud services, online content and international subsea traffic.
“Demand for fast, reliable connectivity is growing rapidly. This investment shows how Openreach is strengthening its network to support wholesale customers across the UK,” said Nicolas Lemaitre, director of products, Openreach. “By using Ciena’s Waveserver and WL6 technology, we’re preparing our services for the next wave of digital growth, including increasing demand from AI applications and Critical National Infrastructure.”
Ciena's partnership with Openreach also extends to helping the broadband provider deploy, proactively monitor, and maintain its OSEA optical product.

Ciena Corporation (NYSE:CIEN) is positioned to benefit from the growing importance of optical networking as artificial intelligence infrastructure expands. As AI data centers scale, the need to move massive volumes of data between GPUs, servers, and data centers is driving demand for faster and higher-bandwidth optical connectivity.
Wall Street’s view on Ciena has shifted sharply. Targets were cut after earnings, then later raised following its 2029 outlook: see the analysis.
Connectivity within and between data centers remains a key challenge as hyperscalers build increasingly large AI clusters to support frontier large language models. According to Evercore ISI analyst Amit Daryanani, Ciena Corporation is well positioned to capitalize on this opportunity.
In a research note to investors on September 21, the analyst upgraded Ciena to an Outperform from In Line, buoyed by its prospects as a dedicated optical systems provider. The analysts also raised the stock’s price target to $550 from $375, insisting it offers an attractive way of gaining exposure to the optical networking space.
The analyst expects the company to be one of the biggest beneficiaries as the data center buildout fuels demand for optical networking systems and high-speed interconnects needed to enhance data transmission between and beyond data centers. It already provides systems capable of transporting massive amounts of data across networks, including between data centers.
Its technology is becoming increasingly important as AI clusters expand beyond individual facilities. Ciena has also introduced its Vesta 200 6.4T co-packaged optical engine, designed for high-density AI networking.
Backed by robust optical networking technology, the company expects revenue to grow at an annual rate of about 30% over the next three years, with adjusted gross margin reaching approximately 50% by fiscal 2029.
The combination of AI-driven data traffic, hyperscaler infrastructure spending, and the transition toward higher-speed optical connectivity could provide Ciena with a significant growth runway.
While the company is benefiting from strong AI-related demand, the stock remains vulnerable to earnings or valuation reset. The market is already pricing in a prolonged AI-driven optical networking boom. Given extremely high AI expectations, the stock could come under pressure if hyperscaler spending falls short.
Supply constraints could also limit the company’s ability to capitalize on strong demand fully. While industrywide constraints can support backlog growth, shortages of components and other inputs could delay converting orders into revenue.
Competition represents another risk. The attractive economics surrounding AI infrastructure could encourage additional investment from networking and optical technology providers, potentially increasing pricing pressure and limiting Ciena’s share of the market.
Insider Monkey database indicates that institutional positioning has been building up around the stock. The number of hedge funds holding Ciena Corporation shares rose to 81 in the second quarter, up from 73 in the first quarter. Arrowstreet Capital increased its stake in the company by 21% to $822.68 million, while AQR Capital Management increased its stake by 8% to $507.24 million.
Meanwhile, the amount of Ciena shares sold short dropped to 3.35 million as of August 31 from 3.71 million as of July 31, translating to a short interest of 2.36%.
Ciena Corporation offers investors exposure to the growing demand for optical networking amid robust AI data center buildout. The company’s optical systems and next-generation technologies could position it to benefit from the continued expansion of AI infrastructure.
The key question for investors is whether Ciena can translate the rapid expansion of AI-related networking demand into sustained revenue and margin growth without market expectations running too far ahead of fundamentals.

Networking Stocks Rally as Tech Rebound Lifts AI Gear Makers: Ciena and Arista Climb 4%, but Cisco Barely Moves
AI data center spending is splitting networking stocks into clear winners and laggards, and the gap between Ciena, Arista, and Cisco reveals which part of the network hyperscalers are actually racing to build.
Published October 19, 2026, 2:06pm ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
Networking hardware is leading a broad technology rebound, and suppliers of optical links and Ethernet switches for AI data centers are drawing the biggest buying. By Monday afternoon, Ciena Corporation (NYSE:CIEN | CIEN Price Prediction) stock was up 4% to $347.48. Meanwhile, Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) stock also climbed 4%, hitting $183.32 and keeping pace with the gain in Ciena shares.
Shares of Ciena and Arista are running well ahead of the wider technology group. The iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is up 1.29%. Large-cap tech is advancing at a similar pace, with the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) also up 1.31%.
A sharp pullback in Ciena and Arista shares over the prior week came before the bounce. Hyperscaler spending on AI infrastructure remains the core support for Ciena and Arista. Both companies build the networks that move data between and inside AI data centers.
Supply Limits Keep Ciena’s Backlog Growing
Ciena’s fiscal Q3 2026 results showed adjusted EPS of $2.11 against a $1.73 consensus. The company’s revenue rose 37% year over year (YoY) to $1.67 billion.
Cloud providers did the biggest spending for Ciena, accounting for 53% of revenue on 82% YoY growth. Management raised its fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to $6.42 billion and issued a preliminary fiscal 2027 outlook calling for at least 30% revenue growth.
Strong demand also shows in Ciena’s backlog, as the company ended Q3 with $8.5 billion on the books and projects to exit fiscal 2026 with over $10 billion. During the earnings call, executives stated, “The demand is absolutely there.” Supply remains the limit, and management doesn’t projects the market to return to balance before 2028.
Optical Links and AI Switches Ride One Spending Wave
Ciena sells optical networking equipment that links data centers, while Arista and Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) sell the switches and routers inside them. Pluggable optics were a standout, with Ciena’s pluggables revenue more than doubling YoY in Q3 as the WaveLogic 6 Nano ramped. Notably, CSCO stock is practically unchanged at $107.06 today, so it’s not keeping pace with CIEN and ANET today.
Arista’s EtherLink switches power Ethernet-based AI fabrics in hyperscale data centers. Management frames the Arista 2.0 strategy around networking. The company sees networking as the “central nervous system” for infrastructure, and EtherLink adoption has spread to a broader roster of cloud, AI and neocloud customers.
Scale-across networks, which connect AI training clusters spread over multiple data centers, are Ciena’s next growth leg. Its RLS HyperRail line system, co-created with hyperscalers, is on track for initial customer adoption by year-end and material revenue through 2027. Co-packaged optics offer another lever, with revenue projects to begin in 2027 and grow into 2028 for Ciena.
Improving operating leverage is showing up in Ciena’s results too, with adjusted gross margin expanding 450 basis points YoY to 46.4%. The company’s chief executive asserted in the earnings release that “AI continues to drive compounding waves of network investment.”
Ciena’s growth carries concentration risk, since two customers made up 41.7% of its Q3 revenue. Its outlook also assumes continued AI infrastructure spending by cloud providers, stable optical component supply and no material change to tariff policy.
Next quarter’s results could show whether Ciena can hit its fiscal Q4 2026 revenue guidance of $1.75 billion under tight component supply. Traders will be tracking whether Ciena and Arista shares keep outpacing the iShares U.S. Technology ETF and the Invesco QQQ Trust.
Long-term supplier agreements running through 2029 could ease Ciena’s bottleneck, though recent moves in its shares show how quickly sentiment can turn. Investors may want to hold smaller share stakes until the supply squeeze resolves.

Ciena Fell 40%—Now One Analyst Sees 50% Upside
Sam Quirke - MarketBeat - Wed Sep 23, 1:30PM CDT
Despite all the money pouring into the artificial intelligence boom, it feels like only a small handful of names have been consistent winners.
Plenty of companies quietly making that boom possible have been overlooked, their shares languishing while the giants soar. Ciena Corporation (NYSE: CIEN) is a good example.
Despite sitting right in the path of the AI wave, its stock has nonetheless tumbled more than 40% from its June high. However, that disconnect may be correcting itself.
After a punishing slide, the stock appears to have found a floor early this month and has started to turn higher, climbing around 17% in less than three weeks.
Even after its fall, Ciena is still up roughly 50% for the year, and the current bounce suggests investors are beginning to look again at a name they had written off. A well-timed vote of confidence from Wall Street this week has helped, making this a perfect time to ask if the market has been way too negative on Ciena’s prospects.
That vote of confidence came from Evercore ISI, with analyst Amit Daryanani upgrading Ciena to Outperform earlier this week and setting a $550 price target. From where the stock trades today, that's around 50% upside, and just as importantly, Daryanani's argument cuts to the heart of the bull case: that Ciena sits at one of the AI boom's most overlooked bottlenecks.
This bottleneck theory is simple. Amid all the noise about chips and computing power, far less attention goes to how that data actually moves around. Modern AI systems shuttle staggering volumes of information between and within data centers, and doing so fast enough has become a serious constraint on how powerful they can be. Daryanani pinpointed connectivity as an increasingly critical bottleneck to the pace of AI's advancement.
This is Ciena's world. The company specializes in optical networking, the high-speed connections that carry data over long distances and, increasingly, across the sprawling AI facilities springing up everywhere. As one of the few dedicated names in the field, it’s particularly well placed to benefit as those systems, and their data demands, keep growing.
The bullish case is more than a story, because the numbers behind it are seriously impressive. In its most recent quarterly report, released earlier this month, Ciena reported year-on-year revenue growth of 37% and earnings per share growth of 215%.
More telling still is the pipeline of future work. Ciena’s management pointed to a swelling order book, with its backlog expected to top $10 billion by the end of its financial year, giving it, and the market, solid visibility into future revenue.
Ciena is also pushing into new territory. Beyond its traditional strength in long-distance links, it's developing products that operate inside data centers themselves, chasing a market it believes could be worth many billions. With leading technology and a clutch of new products, it has several ways to win rather than relying on a single one.
None of this means the risks have vanished. The stock's steep fall from its June high and the volatility that followed remind us how quickly sentiment can turn on a name like this. The biggest worry is simply that the AI spending spree may not last, and Ciena's fortunes are tightly bound to how much the cloud giants keep investing, so any slowdown would hit its orders hard.
There’s also the matter of who its customers are. A handful of large clients account for a hefty slice of Ciena's revenue, with one customer alone making up close to 20%. Such concentration cuts both ways: it’s fine while those customers spend freely, but it would hurt if even one pulled back.
Weighing it up, Ciena makes a compelling case as an underappreciated way to play the AI infrastructure boom. It sits at a real bottleneck, its core business is growing fast, its order book offers rare visibility, and Wall Street is clearly leaning toward the upside.
The caution comes not from the bulls but from the setup itself. Ciena's shares remain volatile, its valuation demands strong growth for years to come, and expectations will likely stay high after this week's upgrade. That tension, between an early-stage turnaround and a business with a lot still to prove, is what keeps the stock finely balanced.
For those who believe the AI buildout has years left to run, though, Ciena increasingly looks like one of its more overlooked beneficiaries, and this week's upgrade is a clear sign that others are already catching on.

AI networking demand is lifting Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET | ANET Price Prediction), Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) and Ciena (NYSE:CIEN), with shares of the optical supplier pulling far ahead of the two switching vendors. No company announcement accounts for the gain in Arista stock, which sits inside a broader bid across networking and optical equipment. That leaves the relative size of the three moves as the clearest signal of where the market sees demand outrunning supply.
Ciena stock is at $431.18, up 11% in midday trading, the largest gain of the three by a wide margin. Meanwhile, Arista Networks stock is at $214.34, up 4%, the smallest advance in the group. Cisco stock trades at $115.83, up 3%, landing between the other two.
For context, the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is up 0.63%, a modest gain for the broader tech sector. At the same time, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.76%. Against those benchmarks, shares of Ciena, Arista and Cisco are each running well ahead of both the tech sector and the overall market, a sign that the buying is targeted at network equipment.
Bernstein Note Ties Networking to Optical
On October 1, Bernstein initiated coverage of Arista Networks with an Outperform rating and a price target of $250, arguing that networking and optical suppliers both benefit from AI infrastructure spending, with demand still running ahead of supply. That note is several days old and serves as background to the session. The detail that matters now is the note’s pairing of networking with optical, since shares of Ciena, the optical name in this group, are running hardest.
Arista Networks reported its second-quarter 2026 results in early August, with revenue growth of 37.7% from a year earlier. Demand across AI networking, data centers, campus and routing drove that growth, giving the company several engines working at once, and such breadth underpins Arista’s longer-term story, though the August report isn’t fresh news for the stock and doesn’t explain the latest buying on its own.
Transport Layer Shows Where Scarcity Sits
Inside data centers, Arista and Cisco sell the switches and routers that move traffic, while Ciena supplies the optical transport layer that carries traffic between those facilities. A buildout that adds computing capacity in more locations lifts transport demand before it lifts switching demand. That sequencing is the structural reason Ciena, Arista and Cisco shares don’t move in lockstep, even when the same AI theme is driving all three.
Ciena stock running several times harder than Arista stock points to the transport layer as the place where the market currently sees scarcity. Bernstein’s note collapsed exactly that distinction by grouping networking and optical suppliers together under one spending thesis. Arista stock is the smallest mover of the three, which complicates reading the session as a story about Arista itself.
Between those extremes, Cisco stock is advancing solidly, which suggests the bid extends across the equipment layer as a whole. The middle slot held by Cisco stock also gives the market a useful reference point, since a broad rally lifts the diversified networking giant while the sharpest gains collect in optical transport. Such a pattern fits a market rewarding AI infrastructure broadly. It reserves its biggest premium for the scarcest piece (we profiled seven of these non-chip AI suppliers, from networking to power and cooling, in a free report you can grab here).
Evidence that switching demand is tightening the way transport demand appears to be would tie the next move in Arista stock to the company specifically, and this session doesn’t supply it. Traders could look for signs that Arista faces the same supply pressure Bernstein described across networking and optical suppliers. Until then, Ciena stock remains a clearer expression of the transport scarcity the market is pricing.
Shareholders may want to keep an eye on whether Cisco stock continues advancing alongside Ciena and Arista, since a sustained broad rally would support the view that AI networking spending is lifting every tier of the equipment stack. A fade in CSCO stock while CIEN stock holds its gains would point to a narrower trade concentrated in optical transport. Either outcome may clarify whether the equipment rally has staying power beyond the optical names.
Ciena stock carries the most risk of the three if transport scarcity eases, since it is running so far ahead of the group, while Arista and Cisco shares are riding the same spending wave with smaller swings. Investors weighing their exposure should calibrate their holdings carefully given that a sector-wide bid across networking and optical equipment is driving all three stocks. Keeping their positions in any one of these names moderate limits how much their portfolios lean on a single tier of the AI networking buildout.

What Was Ciena Telling You Before Its Stock Ran?
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 6:48 AM CDT 3 min read
Ciena (CIEN) stock returned 101.5% from October 16, 2025 to October 19, 2026, against 17.4% for the S&P 500. The run turned out to be about cloud providers and data centers ordering more of Ciena's optical networking gear than the company could ship. The rise began earlier, however. Shares had already risen 184% in the six months before that window opened. So what was Ciena telling investors before April 2025, when its shares still traded near $60?
On its fiscal Q4 2024 call, held December 12, 2024, management said "orders in the quarter were once again above revenue." Orders that outpace revenue move into backlog, representing sales booked but not yet shipped. By the end of that fiscal year, management placed Ciena's backlog at $2.1 billion.
This mattered because sales were standing still. Revenue in the quarter ended November 2, 2024, was $1.12 billion, flat from a year earlier. Management also said customers were working through accumulated inventory, so a reader could see orders stacking up behind a pause in shipments.

How Ciena's Orders Turned Into Sales In 2025
Management said on its fiscal Q1 2025 call, held March 11, 2025, that service providers had largely finished digesting that inventory. It also pointed to rapidly increasing demand for bandwidth driven by cloud connectivity. Reported sales were growing fast within two quarters. Revenue rose 23.6% from a year earlier in the quarter ended May 3, 2025. Growth reached 29.4% in the quarter ended August 2, 2025, and management said on the September 4, 2025, call that revenue came in above the top end of its guidance.
Ciena agreed on September 22, 2025, to acquire Nubis Communications, a maker of optical and electrical interconnects for AI workloads, to expand its business inside the data center. The December 2024 and March 2025 calls both took place before April 2025, while the sales gains and the Nubis deal occurred as the shares were already rising. The clearest signs were therefore public well before the measured window opened on October 16, 2025, and a reader who acted on them in early 2025 would have held the shares through both rises.

Cisco Systems, Arista Networks and Broadcom all returned less than Ciena over the same window, with the best of them returning 57.0%. The sign from December 2024 is still there. On its fiscal Q3 2026 call, held September 3, 2026, management said orders were again well ahead of sales, and Ciena ended that quarter with $8.5 billion in backlog. Management expects backlog of more than $10 billion by the end of fiscal 2026. Ciena's backlog is the figure to watch in the fiscal fourth quarter report, expected on or around December 9, 2026.

Ciena's Openreach Deal: Can 1.6Tb/s Technology Drive Its Growth?
Ciena Corporation CIEN is strengthening its position in the optical networking market as rising demand for high-capacity connectivity drives investments in digital infrastructure. Its latest deployment with Openreach, a major U.K. telecommunications network provider, highlights an opportunity to capitalize on growing bandwidth requirements across data centers, telecommunications networks and international subsea connections.
Openreach is deploying Ciena's Waveserver platform, powered by WaveLogic 6 (WL6) 1.6Tb/s coherent technology, as part of its Optical Spectrum Extended Access (OSEA) portfolio. The solution will enable Openreach to offer wholesale customers tailored, high-capacity network services across the U.K., including connectivity for cable landing stations, data centers and core network nodes. The deployment combines 400G and 800G client traffic over dedicated 1.6Tb/s wavelengths, with a compact 2RU chassis supporting up to 32 400G services. It enables Openreach to introduce national 800G services while providing a pathway to even higher speeds as bandwidth requirements increase. These capabilities could strengthen demand for Ciena's optical networking solutions as network operators seek to transfer larger volumes of data efficiently.
As AI applications increase the need for high-bandwidth connections between data centers and other network endpoints, Ciena's optical technology can help network operators accommodate rising traffic while scaling capacity to meet evolving requirements. Beyond AI, growing online content consumption, cloud adoption and international subsea traffic provide additional demand drivers. These applications broaden the potential market for Ciena's solutions and underscore the importance of upgrading optical networks.
Despite favorable industry trends, Ciena faces competition from other optical networking vendors like Corning Incorporated GLW and Nokia NOK, targeting telecommunications operators and data center customers.
CIEN's Market Position Faces Competitive Pressure
GLW entered the second half of 2026 with its growth outlook tied to AI infrastructure and optical connectivity. Corning is also expanding its GenAI optical portfolio with multicore fiber and high-density connectivity solutions that improve network capacity and reduce installation complexity. It announced a long-term partnership with NVIDIA to expand U.S.-based optical connectivity manufacturing capacity by 10 times and increase domestic fiber production capacity by more than 50%. In September, Corning secured a multi-year, multibillion-dollar Verizon deal to supply more than 80 million miles of optical fiber through 2032, boosting revenue visibility and exposure to broadband and AI infrastructure demand.
NOK continues to benefit from its broad portfolio spanning mobile networks, optical transport, IP routing, fixed broadband, software and services. Network Infrastructure delivered double-digit growth in second-quarter 2026, supported by continued momentum in Optical Networks and IP Networks. The planned divestiture of the Fixed Wireless Access CPE business simplifies the portfolio and allows greater investment in higher-growth opportunities such as AI networking and optical technologies. NOK is also expanding U.S. optical manufacturing capacity through investments in San Jose, PA and the planned acquisition of an additional semiconductor manufacturing site in Arizona. Management noted that supply constraints persist in optical networking, supporting long-term customer orders.

Networking hardware is leading a broad technology rebound, and suppliers of optical links and Ethernet switches for AI data centers are drawing the biggest buying. By Monday afternoon, Ciena Corporation (NYSE:CIEN | CIEN Price Prediction) stock was up 4% to $347.48. Meanwhile, Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) stock also climbed 4%, hitting $183.32 and keeping pace with the gain in Ciena shares.
Shares of Ciena and Arista are running well ahead of the wider technology group. The iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is up 1.29%. Large-cap tech is advancing at a similar pace, with the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) also up 1.31%.
A sharp pullback in Ciena and Arista shares over the prior week came before the bounce. Hyperscaler spending on AI infrastructure remains the core support for Ciena and Arista. Both companies build the networks that move data between and inside AI data centers.
Supply Limits Keep Ciena’s Backlog Growing
Ciena’s fiscal Q3 2026 results showed adjusted EPS of $2.11 against a $1.73 consensus. The company’s revenue rose 37% year over year (YoY) to $1.67 billion.
Cloud providers did the biggest spending for Ciena, accounting for 53% of revenue on 82% YoY growth. Management raised its fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to $6.42 billion and issued a preliminary fiscal 2027 outlook calling for at least 30% revenue growth.
Strong demand also shows in Ciena’s backlog, as the company ended Q3 with $8.5 billion on the books and projects to exit fiscal 2026 with over $10 billion. During the earnings call, executives stated, “The demand is absolutely there.” Supply remains the limit, and management doesn’t projects the market to return to balance before 2028.
Optical Links and AI Switches Ride One Spending Wave
Ciena sells optical networking equipment that links data centers, while Arista and Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) sell the switches and routers inside them. Pluggable optics were a standout, with Ciena’s pluggables revenue more than doubling YoY in Q3 as the WaveLogic 6 Nano ramped. Notably, CSCO stock is practically unchanged at $107.06 today, so it’s not keeping pace with CIEN and ANET today.
Arista’s EtherLink switches power Ethernet-based AI fabrics in hyperscale data centers. Management frames the Arista 2.0 strategy around networking. The company sees networking as the “central nervous system” for infrastructure, and EtherLink adoption has spread to a broader roster of cloud, AI and neocloud customers.
Scale-across networks, which connect AI training clusters spread over multiple data centers, are Ciena’s next growth leg. Its RLS HyperRail line system, co-created with hyperscalers, is on track for initial customer adoption by year-end and material revenue through 2027. Co-packaged optics offer another lever, with revenue projects to begin in 2027 and grow into 2028 for Ciena.
Improving operating leverage is showing up in Ciena’s results too, with adjusted gross margin expanding 450 basis points YoY to 46.4%. The company’s chief executive asserted in the earnings release that “AI continues to drive compounding waves of network investment.”
Ciena’s growth carries concentration risk, since two customers made up 41.7% of its Q3 revenue. Its outlook also assumes continued AI infrastructure spending by cloud providers, stable optical component supply and no material change to tariff policy.
Next quarter’s results could show whether Ciena can hit its fiscal Q4 2026 revenue guidance of $1.75 billion under tight component supply. Traders will be tracking whether Ciena and Arista shares keep outpacing the iShares U.S. Technology ETF and the Invesco QQQ Trust.
Long-term supplier agreements running through 2029 could ease Ciena’s bottleneck, though recent moves in its shares show how quickly sentiment can turn. Investors may want to hold smaller share stakes until the supply squeeze resolves.

Ciena Fell 40%—Now One Analyst Sees 50% Upside

Despite all the money pouring into the artificial intelligence boom, it feels like only a small handful of names have been consistent winners.
Plenty of companies quietly making that boom possible have been overlooked, their shares languishing while the giants soar. Ciena Corporation (NYSE: CIEN) is a good example.
Despite sitting right in the path of the AI wave, its stock has nonetheless tumbled more than 40% from its June high. However, that disconnect may be correcting itself.
After a punishing slide, the stock appears to have found a floor early this month and has started to turn higher, climbing around 17% in less than three weeks.
Even after its fall, Ciena is still up roughly 50% for the year, and the current bounce suggests investors are beginning to look again at a name they had written off. A well-timed vote of confidence from Wall Street this week has helped, making this a perfect time to ask if the market has been way too negative on Ciena’s prospects.
That vote of confidence came from Evercore ISI, with analyst Amit Daryanani upgrading Ciena to Outperform earlier this week and setting a $550 price target. From where the stock trades today, that's around 50% upside, and just as importantly, Daryanani's argument cuts to the heart of the bull case: that Ciena sits at one of the AI boom's most overlooked bottlenecks.
This bottleneck theory is simple. Amid all the noise about chips and computing power, far less attention goes to how that data actually moves around. Modern AI systems shuttle staggering volumes of information between and within data centers, and doing so fast enough has become a serious constraint on how powerful they can be. Daryanani pinpointed connectivity as an increasingly critical bottleneck to the pace of AI's advancement.
This is Ciena's world. The company specializes in optical networking, the high-speed connections that carry data over long distances and, increasingly, across the sprawling AI facilities springing up everywhere. As one of the few dedicated names in the field, it’s particularly well placed to benefit as those systems, and their data demands, keep growing.
The bullish case is more than a story, because the numbers behind it are seriously impressive. In its most recent quarterly report, released earlier this month, Ciena reported year-on-year revenue growth of 37% and earnings per share growth of 215%.
More telling still is the pipeline of future work. Ciena’s management pointed to a swelling order book, with its backlog expected to top $10 billion by the end of its financial year, giving it, and the market, solid visibility into future revenue.
Ciena is also pushing into new territory. Beyond its traditional strength in long-distance links, it's developing products that operate inside data centers themselves, chasing a market it believes could be worth many billions. With leading technology and a clutch of new products, it has several ways to win rather than relying on a single one.
None of this means the risks have vanished. The stock's steep fall from its June high and the volatility that followed remind us how quickly sentiment can turn on a name like this. The biggest worry is simply that the AI spending spree may not last, and Ciena's fortunes are tightly bound to how much the cloud giants keep investing, so any slowdown would hit its orders hard.
There’s also the matter of who its customers are. A handful of large clients account for a hefty slice of Ciena's revenue, with one customer alone making up close to 20%. Such concentration cuts both ways: it’s fine while those customers spend freely, but it would hurt if even one pulled back.
Weighing it up, Ciena makes a compelling case as an underappreciated way to play the AI infrastructure boom. It sits at a real bottleneck, its core business is growing fast, its order book offers rare visibility, and Wall Street is clearly leaning toward the upside.
The caution comes not from the bulls but from the setup itself. Ciena's shares remain volatile, its valuation demands strong growth for years to come, and expectations will likely stay high after this week's upgrade. That tension, between an early-stage turnaround and a business with a lot still to prove, is what keeps the stock finely balanced.
For those who believe the AI buildout has years left to run, though, Ciena increasingly looks like one of its more overlooked beneficiaries, and this week's upgrade is a clear sign that others are already catching on.

On October 1, Bernstein initiated coverage of Arista Networks with an Outperform rating and a price target of $250, arguing that networking and optical suppliers both benefit from AI infrastructure spending, with demand still running ahead of supply. The detail that matters now is the note’s pairing of networking with optical, since shares of Ciena, the optical name in this group, are running hardest.
Arista Networks reported its second-quarter 2026 results in early August, with revenue growth of 37.7% from a year earlier. Demand across AI networking, data centers, campus and routing drove that growth, giving the company several engines working at once, and such breadth underpins Arista’s longer-term story, though the August report isn’t fresh news for the stock and doesn’t explain the latest buying on its own.
Transport Layer Shows Where Scarcity Sits
Inside data centers, Arista and Cisco sell the switches and routers that move traffic, while Ciena supplies the optical transport layer that carries traffic between those facilities. A buildout that adds computing capacity in more locations lifts transport demand before it lifts switching demand. That sequencing is the structural reason Ciena, Arista and Cisco shares don’t move in lockstep, even when the same AI theme is driving all three.
Ciena stock running several times harder than Arista stock points to the transport layer as the place where the market currently sees scarcity. Bernstein’s note collapsed exactly that distinction by grouping networking and optical suppliers together under one spending thesis. Arista stock is the smallest mover of the three, which complicates reading the session as a story about Arista itself.
Between those extremes, Cisco stock is advancing solidly, which suggests the bid extends across the equipment layer as a whole. Traders could look for signs that Arista faces the same supply pressure Bernstein described across networking and optical suppliers. Shareholders may want to keep an eye on whether Cisco stock continues advancing alongside Ciena and Arista, since a sustained broad rally would support the view that AI networking spending is lifting every tier of the equipment stack. A fade in CSCO stock while CIEN stock holds its gains would point to a narrower trade concentrated in optical transport. Either outcome may clarify whether the equipment rally has staying power beyond the optical names.
Ciena stock carries the most risk of the three if transport scarcity eases, since it is running so far ahead of the group, while Arista and Cisco shares are riding the same spending wave with smaller swings. Ciena Corporation Announces Pricing of Upsized Convertible Senior Notes
2026 – Ciena® Corporation (NYSE: CIEN) (the “Company”), the global leader in high-speed connectivity, today announced that it has
priced its private offering (the “Offering”) of $2.5 billion aggregate principal amount of 0.00% convertible senior notes due 2031 (the “Notes”). The Notes will be fully and unconditionally guaranteed, on a senior
unsecured basis, by each wholly-owned domestic subsidiary of Ciena that currently or in the future guarantees its 4.00% senior notes due 2030 or any refinancing of such notes (the “guarantees”). The size of the Offering was
increased from the previously announced $2.0 billion aggregate principal amount of Notes. The Company also granted to the initial purchasers of the Notes an option to purchase up to an additional $375.0 million aggregate principal amount
of the Notes within a 13-day period beginning on, and including, the first date on which the Notes are issued. The Offering and the convertible note hedge and warrant transactions described below are expected
to close on June 11, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. The closing of the Offering is not contingent upon the closing of such convertible note hedge and warrant transactions.
The Company intends to use (i) $100.0 million of the net proceeds from the Offering to pay the net cost of the convertible note hedge transactions
described below (after such cost is partially offset by the proceeds of the Company’s entry into the warrant transactions described below) and (ii) approximately $140.0 million of the net proceeds to repurchase approximately
0.3 million shares of the Company’s common stock concurrently with the Offering in privately negotiated transactions effected with or through one of the initial purchasers or its affiliate, at a purchase price per share equal to the last
reported sale price of $466.67 per share of the Company’s common stock on the New York Stock Exchange (“NYSE”) on June 8, 2026. The Company intends to use approximately $1.14 billion of the remaining net proceeds from the
Offering to repay amounts outstanding under its term loan under its existing credit facility and pay related fees and expenses. The Company intends to use the remainder of the net proceeds for general corporate purposes, including investments to
enhance supply chain capacity.
The concurrent repurchases of shares of the Company’s common stock described above may result in the Company’s
common stock trading at prices that are higher than would be the case in the absence of these repurchases, which may have resulted in a higher initial conversion price for the Notes. In addition, any repurchases of the Company’s common stock
following the Offering could affect the trading price of the Notes and, if conducted during an observation period for the conversion of any Notes, could affect the number of shares and value of the consideration that is due upon such conversion.
Potential hedging activity in connection with the convertible note hedge and warrant transactions described below may also affect the market price of the Company’s common stock or the Notes, holders’ ability to convert the Notes or the
number of shares and value of the consideration to be received upon conversion of the Notes as described below.
The Notes will be senior unsecured obligations of the Company. The Notes will not bear regular interest and
the principal amount of the Notes will not accrete. The Notes will mature on September 15, 2031, unless earlier converted, redeemed or repurchased. The initial conversion rate for the Notes is 1.3393 shares of the Company’s common stock
per $1,000 principal amount of Notes (equivalent to an initial conversion price of approximately $746.66 per share of the Company’s common stock), which represents a conversion premium of approximately 60.0% percent over the last reported sale
price of $466.67 per share of the Company’s common stock on the NYSE on June 8, 2026.
Prior to June 15, 2031, the Notes will be
convertible only upon satisfaction of certain conditions and during certain periods, and thereafter, the Notes will be convertible at any time until the close of business on the second scheduled trading day immediately preceding the maturity date.
The Company will satisfy any conversion by paying cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the Notes to be converted and by paying or delivering, as the case may be, cash, shares of the Company’s common stock or a combination of cash and
shares of the Company’s common stock, at its election, in respect of the remainder, if any, of its conversion obligation in excess of the aggregate principal amount of the Notes being converted. The Company may not redeem the Notes prior to
September 20, 2029, except in the event of a cleanup redemption (as defined below). The Notes will be redeemable, in whole or in part, at the Company’s option on or after September 20, 2029, upon the satisfaction of certain
conditions and subject to certain limitations. In addition, the Notes will be redeemable at any time if the aggregate principal amount of the Notes that remains outstanding is less than 10% of the aggregate principal amount of the Notes initially
issued in the Offering and certain other conditions are satisfied (a “cleanup redemption”).
In connection with the pricing of the Notes, the
Company has entered into convertible note hedge transactions with certain of the initial purchasers of the Notes or their respective affiliates and certain other financial institutions (the “option counterparties”). These transactions
cover, subject to anti-dilution adjustments substantially similar to those applicable to the Notes, the same number of shares of the Company’s common stock that will initially underlie the Notes, and are expected generally to reduce any
dilutive effect on the Company’s common stock of the Notes and/or offset any cash payments the Company is required to make in excess of the principal amount of converted Notes, as the case may be. Concurrently with entry into the convertible
note hedge transactions, the Company has also entered into warrant transactions with the option counterparties relating to the same number of shares of the Company’s common stock, subject to customary anti-dilution adjustments. The strike
price of the warrant transactions will initially be $1,000.00 per share, which represents an approximate 114.3% premium to the last reported sale price of the Company’s common stock on the NYSE on June 8, 2026. The warrant transactions
could separately have a dilutive effect on the Company’s common stock to the extent that the market price per share of the Company’s common stock exceeds the strike price of the warrants.
If the initial purchasers exercise their option to purchase additional Notes, the Company expects to enter into additional convertible note hedge transactions
and additional warrant transactions with the option counterparties.
The Company has been advised by the option counterparties that, in connection with establishing their initial
hedges of the convertible note hedge and warrant transactions, the option counterparties or their respective affiliates expect to enter into various derivative transactions with respect to the Company’s common stock and/or purchase shares of
the Company’s common stock concurrently with or shortly after the pricing of the Notes. This activity could increase (or reduce the size of any decrease in) the market price of the Company’s common stock and/or the Notes at that time.
The option counterparties or their respective affiliates may also modify their hedge positions by entering into or unwinding various derivatives with respect to the Company’s common stock and/or purchasing or selling the Company’s common
stock or other securities of the Company in secondary market transactions following the pricing of the Notes and prior to the maturity of the Notes (and are likely to do so in connection with any conversion of the Notes, any redemption of Notes, any
repurchase of the Notes upon a fundamental change or any other repurchase of Notes if the Company elects to terminate a corresponding portion of the convertible note hedge transactions). This activity could also cause or avoid an increase or a
decrease in the market price of the Company’s common stock and/or the Notes, which could affect the ability of holders to convert the Notes and, to the extent the activity occurs during any observation period related to a conversion of the
Notes, it could affect the number of shares and value of the consideration that noteholders will receive upon conversion of the Notes.
